standard_prerequisites.use: Organises the finitely presented approximations into a directed system whose colimit is M.

core_obligations: Index the approximation by a finite subset S of M together with a finite collection E of relations among its elements (proof lines 1855-1859).
Define M_{S,E} as the cokernel of the map between finite free modules encoded by those relations, which is finitely presented, and note the canonical maps to M (proof lines 1860-1865).
Make the index set directed by inclusion of this data and observe that the resulting colimit is M (proof lines 1866-1872).
proof_roadmap: Encode finite presentations by finite sets of elements and relations (proof lines 1854-1864).
Order these data by inclusion and take the colimit (proof lines 1865-1873).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every module is the colimit of a directed system of finitely presented modules (statement lines 1846-1852). The proof does not invoke a general presentability theorem: it indexes the approximation by pairs consisting of a finite subset of M and a finite collection of relations among them, defines each approximating module as the cokernel of the map between finite free modules encoded by those relations, and orders the pairs by inclusion so that the colimit is visibly M (proof lines 1854-1873). Finding the right index set, so that both finite presentation and directedness come out at once, is the content of the construction. H2.
